 Ajay Mitchell had 23 points (9-of-17 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Cavaliers on Wednesday. 
 While the Thunder are without multiple starters, it appears they’ll be counting on Mitchell for significant scoring. He has at least 20 points in four of his last five games, showing he may be up to the challenge. Mitchell’s fantasy floor has certainly risen given his situation. OKC will have the day off Thursday before taking on the Grizzlies Friday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Ajay Mitchell

 Ajay Mitchell had 20 points (7-of-16 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, one assist and one block against the Cavaliers on Monday. 
 Mitchell appears to be the main beneficiary of the injuries the Thunder are dealing with. The 24-year-old guard took more shots and played more minutes than all of his teammates besides Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on Monday. Until the Thunder are back to full strength, fantasy managers can expect that to continue. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell had 29 points (12-of-20 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Mitchell moved into the starting lineup Monday with the Thunder dealing with a number of injuries and dropped a career-high 30 points in the win over the Suns. He scored 29 points Wednesday against the Mavericks, though it still wasn’t enough to prevent a blowout loss. Nevertheless, Mitchell has become a must-roster player and potentially a league-winner as he continues to produce at a high level when given increased opportunities. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Initially questionable for Wednesday’s game, Mitchell is now available. Because of Oklahoma City’s injuries, he should be rostered in most redraft leagues. Mitchell is coming off his first 30-point game in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is quesitonable for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Less than 24 hours after dropping a career-high 30 points on the Suns, Mitchell is on the Thunder injury report with a sprained right ankle. Given the absences Oklahoma City is already dealing with, Mitchell’s absence would significantly affect the team’s rotation. Bennett Stirtz, who played 25 minutes on Monday, could be asked to take on a larger role, possibly as a starter. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell went off for 30 points (10-of-16 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 With Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) out for the foreseeable future, the Thunder will need greater contributions from players like Mitchell to stay afloat in the West. The third-year guard started on Monday and delivered the best game of his NBA career to date. Mitchell finished with his first 30-point game and was a steal shy of a complete stat line. If Mitchell is still on your league’s waiver wire, add him immediately. 
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 The Thunder have three new starters for Monday’s game, and two (McCain and Mitchell) could hold onto those roles for the foreseeable future. Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) could miss the rest of the season due to injuries that require surgery. “Kenny Hustle” starts for Chet Holmgren, who is dealing with right patellar tendinitis. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Cason Wallace will undergo surgery to repair a left labrum tear. 
 Wallace had already been ruled out for Monday’s game following an early exit on Sunday, but it now appears the injury is going to keep him sidelined a while longer. The hits just keep coming for OKC, with Jalen Williams (leg) set to have surgery as well. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain will both take on significant roles until Wallace and/or Williams return. 
 Jalen Williams 
 OKC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #8 
 Jalen Williams has suffered a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle. 
 Williams’s injury was gruesome, and this diagnosis confirms it. General manager Sam Presti said a timeline will be provided following the surgery, but at this time, it’s unclear exactly how long he’ll be out. However, given the severity, it’s safe to say it will be a lengthy absence for him. Jared McCain and Ajay Mitchell should both take on larger roles with Cason Wallace (shoulder) set to undergo surgery as well. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Cason Wallace (shoulder) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Wallace left Sunday’s game with a shoulder injury and didn’t return. He’ll subsequently miss Monday’s game against the Bucks. Ajay Mitchell is certainly a candidate for more minutes and potentially a starting spot with Wallace sidelined. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell accounted for 18 points (8-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Clippers. 
 The Thunder lost Cason Wallace (shoulder) in the first quarter on Sunday. While Mitchell wasn’t the choice to start the third quarter, his role will expand if Wallace misses time. Jared McCain (three points, one rebound, one steal, and one three-pointer) replaced Wallace, and he can provide points and three-pointers in that role. However, Mitchell is the better option for fantasy managers left choosing between the two on the waiver wire.

 Devin Booker had 33 points (9-of-19 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), one rebound, two assists and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday. 
 Booker was just 2-of-8 from behind the three-point line in this one, but made his hay at the foul line as he drained all 13 of his free throw attempts on his way to a 33-point game. The 30-year-old guard played almost 34 minutes despite fouling out for the second consecutive game. Booker and the Suns will be back on the floor Thursday at home against the Magic.

 Reed Sheppard finished Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 14 points (5-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, three steals and three three-pointers.
 Sheppard has now scored in double figures in three of the six games he’s played this season. Against the Timberwolves, his final stat line included a season-high three steals. With the Rockets signing Marcus Smart (four points, one rebound, one assist, one block and one three-pointer) during the offseason and Fred VanVleet back from a torn ACL, Sheppard’s upside in redraft leagues is limited as long as both veterans are healthy.

 Fred VanVleet amassed 18 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Back in the Rockets’ lineup after sitting out Monday’s win over the Celtics, VanVleet played 30 minutes against the Timberwolves. Even though he shot 50 percent from the field on Wednesday, the Rockets’ guard is making just 39 percent of his attempts this season. VanVleet has long offered little value in that category. But most fantasy managers know he’ll do enough across the board to be a solid category-league option.

 RJ Barrett put up 22 points (7-of-17 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, and three 3-pointers in 128-109 loss to the Nuggets.
 Barrett led the team in shot attempts in this game and he did a good job scoring the ball. On the season, he’s averaging 20.9 points, 6 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.5 steals, and 0.5 blocks, shooting 48.1% from the field, 59.5% from the free throw line, and 31.8% from three. Outside of the free throw percentage, he’s been great for where he was selected in redraft leagues. There’s even room for him to get better once he starts hitting more of his free throws.

 Şengün, who has recorded three double-doubles this season, notched his first triple-double on Wednesday.  Lillard has now scored 25 points and had at least five assists in both of his matchups against the Suns so far this season. The 36-year-old point guard played 32 minutes and was +16 in the 13-point win. Portland begins a back-to-back against the Lakers and Spurs Friday in Los Angeles.

 After a testy exchange with a reporter following Monday’s win over the Celtics, Durant attempted 14 shots on Wednesday. The percentages were good and the stat line was solid, with KD logging 35 minutes. One game in which he attempts just six shots should not cause panic among fantasy managers.

 Scottie Barnes got himself 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, six assists, three steals, a three, and five turnovers in loss to Nuggets.
 Scottie filled up the box score despite not having the greatest night scoring the ball. The Raptors as a whole didn’t do a great job defensively in this game which resulted in their blowout. Scottie has had so many good performances recently that there’s no need to panic. The next opportunity to bounce back will be against the Bucks on Friday.

 Jonathan Kuminga produced 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Rockets.
 Anthony Edwards’ knee injury and subsequent surgery created more scoring opportunities for the entire Timberwolves rotation, but Kuminga’s production has been inconsistent. Over the last five games, he’s alternated between single- and double-digit scoring efforts. Given the trend, Kuminga was due for a solid performance on Wednesday, and he recorded a complete stat line. Fantasy managers will hope Kuminga can build on this night when the Timberwolves visit the Pelicans on Friday.
